correctness.rationale: All nonempty connected-shore cuts of K_{p,q} are exactly the complement classes of (i) two nonconstant shore signs or (ii) one exceptional vertex, giving C/2 distinct 0/1 vertices. Their exact two- and four-spin moments imply a 4-class block covariance. The four orthogonal eigenspaces exhaust the pq-dimensional ambient edge space. Differences and a monotone exponential-over-quadratic bound prove strict threshold q_*(p), no ties, and zero eigenvalue only at K_{2,2}. Exact-rational direct enumeration independently verified 19 small pairs, 5133 vertices, 6144 covariance entries, and 102 threshold profiles; finite tests supplement the all-integer proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted public literature and semantic record searches identify graph-bond facet/optimization studies, biclique graphical-zonotope ellipsoid geometry, and biclique spanning-tree-polytope asymmetry. Their statements use different invariants or different polytope vertex sets and do not imply the asserted exact nonempty-bond covariance spectrum or exponentially displaced strict minimum-variance threshold. The original 2020 study includes an optional zero-cut convention: the sampled object here is explicitly different when zero is adjoined. Full historical novelty cannot be certified from searches alone.

value.rationale: This is a complete geometric second-moment invariant, including every eigenspace and its multiplicity, for a natural infinite two-parameter family of connected-cut incidence polytopes. A sharp, exponentially displaced transition of the least-variance eigendirection as the aspect ratio varies is a structural feature that counting bonds or the usual facet description does not provide. The precise exclusion of zero also isolates a natural nonempty-cut sampling law.
